page: Amazon Web Services r5b.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor with an x86_64 architecture, offering 96 virtual CPUs and 48 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz and includes 35 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for AVX-512 vector instructions and AES cryptography.

The instance is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a resource-dense allocation of 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the r5b.24xlarge demonstrates strong multi-core performance, as evidenced by high scores in stress-ng multi-core tests, Passmark CPU extended instructions, and Passmark CPU encryption. Memory performance is highly efficient, with strong read and write bandwidth benchmarks for both small and large blocks. Redis SET operations also rank in the top tier, achieving 74.14 million operations per second. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown in single-threaded stress-ng and gzip compression tests. Large-scale LLM text generation benchmarks also show lower performance.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r5b.24xlarge offers high memory density and strong multi-threaded capabilities, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe storage. It is well-suited for large-scale database operations, in-memory caching systems like Redis, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.
